manifest.summary: This apps/codec-lab/ folder is only a pointer - the real code is the separate git repo at ~/anime-codec-lab (its own .venv, its own Wine cross-build tooling, its own history). Codec Lab is a research harness that races experimental anime-compression ideas against a real AV1 control on the same clip, judged by the same numbers: file size, bits/pixel, PSNR, SSIM, encode/decode time.

features.name: Clip + run setup
features.description: Pick or upload a source clip, set trim/scale/fps, configure any strategy's parameters via a form built from its schema, queue several configs as one batch (a real parameter sweep).

features.name: Automatic control run
features.description: Every batch gets or reuses a fixed AV1 baseline (libsvtav1 crf 30) for that exact clip+trim, so every comparison has a real codec to beat.

features.name: Results database
features.description: SQLite (lab.db): search by strategy/clip/params text, filter by min ratio/PSNR/SSIM, sort any column. Every run ever done persists across restarts; tracks is_control per run.

features.name: Three-way comparison
features.description: Click a row for original vs control codec vs result, each playable with audio; a dropdown swaps in any other completed run against the same clip+trim.

features.name: .acv export
features.description: Package a run's raw encoded bytes + trimmed passthrough audio (WAV) into a standalone .acv file (core/container.py) that Codec Player and player.py can open with no lab, no ffmpeg, no source clip.

features.name: Strategies
features.description: ffmpeg_baseline (control), palette_motion (palette quant + whole-frame-vectorized motion-compensated block copy), downscale_proxy (downscale + codec + sharp upscale - current practical leader), vector_art (per-frame vectorization, no motion), optical_flow (dense Farneback warp + quantized residual - best quality, worst ratio), frame_memory (whole-clip content-addressable block dictionary), temporal_skip (keyframes + flow-interpolated skip frames). Add one by dropping a class in strategies/ and one entry in strategies/registry.py.

manifest.data_dir: resolved by ~/anime-codec-lab/core/paths.py data_dir(): lab.db, results/runs/<id>/ (decoded.mp4, original.mp4, encoded.bin, audio.wav), clips/. Frozen builds put these next to the executable.
services: None networked. Requires ffmpeg + ffprobe at runtime (core/clip_loader.py shells out to load/trim/scale video and mux/extract audio).

required: python-pywebview (system, for the native desktop_app.py window)
optional: intel-compute-runtime - OpenCL / cv2.UMat path in palette_motion (the bigger speed win was algorithmic, see repo README)

manifest.standalone_launch: cd ~/anime-codec-lab && python3 desktop_app.py   (native window; or `uvicorn server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8731` for a browser tab; or `python3 harness.py` for the scriptable CLI). In Forge it runs on port 8431 from the root path.
manifest.memory_guard: core/limits.py projects peak RAM from ffprobe dimensions before allocating. POST /api/runs returns 413 with a suggested scale when a run would exceed the ceiling (default 4 GiB, env CODEC_LAB_RUN_BUDGET_BYTES). Interrupted 'running' rows are reaped to 'interrupted' at startup; resuming is an explicit choice and re-checks the budget. This machine has 31 GiB and no swap, so overshoot freezes it.
known_gaps: Custom formats carry video only - audio is passthrough (muxed onto previews so comparisons are watchable, but no strategy encodes audio).
Localhost / no auth - a personal research tool, not meant past 127.0.0.1.
Two workers process the queue sequentially; a big batch of slow configs queues rather than runs at once.
The identified bottleneck in every custom codec here is the entropy coder (plain zlib), not the prediction idea - fixing residual/entropy coding is the top priority in the repo README.
